children: Microsoft
is expected to post a nearly 17% rise in revenue during the tech giant’s quarterly results on Wednesday, driven by strong cloud growth amid accelerating demand for artificial intelligence services.
Wall Street expects the Redmond, Washington-based firm to
EPS of $4.72, implying a rise of 14%, while revenue is expected to rise nearly 17% to $90.74B during the quarter.
The market’s perception of Microsoft
has strengthened considerably

following the company’s last quarter's results and annual guidance, which signaled sustained growth across its core business segments. The stock gained over 36% since its second quarter earnings report.

Morgan Stanley believes Microsoft needs to show Azure growth in the mid-40s range, along with improved monetization for Microsoft 365 and Copilot, along with “disciplined” operating expenses to keep the momentum going into fiscal 2027.

“We continue to believe the growth construct is in its best place we've seen in quite some time, with a setup for stronger upside and acceleration across both Azure & M365 in the qtrs ahead,” stated TD Cowen analyst Derrick Wood, adding that the brokerage sees potential for a higher than normal beat on Azure.
However, the AI-related sell-off earlier this month highlights growing investor scrutiny over the massive AI investments done by Big Techs, as the market increasingly looks for tangible returns.
Last week, Meta Platforms
saw its stock declining after the company posted higher capital expenditures and guidance that highlighted the scale of the company's ongoing AI infrastructure build-out.

“While recent industry earnings updates corroborate accelerating AI infrastructure demand and improving monetization prospects, ballooning infrastructure spending commitments, alongside widening credit spreads and rising interest rates, are increasingly pivoting the market's focus towards emerging capital constraints,”
a recent Seeking Alpha analysis by Summit Research.

Nevertheless, the analyst added that Microsoft's positive FCF profile, supported by sustained Azure acceleration and resilient profitability, remains a key competitive advantage against its hyperscaler peers.
Microsoft will report under a new structure starting with the first quarter. This time the company’s report will be condensed into two segments: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.

Agents and Infra will include Microsoft 365, GitHub, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, frontier and support services, and Azure. Devices and Consumer will include search, advertising, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices.

and rated the stock a Buy and above. In contrast, Seeking Alpha’s Quant ratings consider it a Hold.
Over the last three months, EPS estimates have seen 18 upward revisions and four downward revisions. Revenue estimates have been revised upwards 31 times versus three downward moves.
The stock has risen over 9% so far this year, compared to the 12% rise in the broader S&P 500 index.
